out.other_title: Prover-Verifier Games: untrusted strong prover, trusted weak verifier, checkable answers
out.rationale: Anil et al. introduce prover-verifier games with one untrusted prover and one trusted verifier on decision problems. Hammond and Adam-Day define a generalised PVG as a messaging game among n_p provers and n_v verifiers on probabilistic decision problems, starting from a common input and ending with a deciding verifier's 0/1 output, so the single-prover, single-verifier game is a special case.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: prover-verifier games for learning checkable protocols, generalised to many provers and verifiers

text: The authors define a generalised prover-verifier game for a probabilistic decision problem as a messaging game played between n_p provers and n_v verifiers, beginning with common observation of an input x drawn from P, in which a deciding verifier outputs 1 or 0. The deciding verifier's loss is ordered by its expected probability of outputting the true label.
title: Generalised prover-verifier game (PVG) defined as a messaging game
